Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Q3 production plan

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this — Lumera is targeting a Q3 production launch for our medical summarization product and we need a dedicated capacity path that aligns with an aggressive rollout. High-level requirements:
- Peak concurrent requests: ~1,200 per minute (short bursts)
- Avg token rate/day: ~300M tokens/day initially, with 3x growth over 6 months
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for 2k token responses
- Models: preference for open-model variants (70B-class) with 8-bit quantization; fallbacks OK
- Compliance: SOC2 + optional VPC/private deployment in future

Can you share 2–3 concrete reservation options (cluster slate definitions) we can include in our procurement packet? We're especially interested in: minimum-activatable GPUs, suggested ramp schedule (weeks/months), warm-pool/burst strategy, and an expected unit cost band (ballpark). Attached is our RFP with usage profiles and SLAs.

Also copying procurement (procurements@lumera.ai). If helpful, happy to set a 30min design call this week.

Thanks,
Anna Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Lumera AI

Hi Anna — great to meet you (virtually) and thanks for the RFP.

I've sketched three pragmatic reservation slates that align with your ramp and latency goals. High-level summary below; I attached a spreadsheet with the line-itemized options.

Option A — Compact Canary
- Cluster: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (8x80GB or equivalent)
- Min activatable GPUs: 6 (can keep 2 hot spare for redundancy)
- Expected throughput: ~120 reqs/min @ 1k token avg; p95 ~300ms for quantized 70B on optimized kernels
- Ramp: Week 0–4: canary (6→8 GPUs), Week 5–12: steady ramp to 12 GPUs if metrics validated
- Warm pool / burst: 2-GPU warm pool, burst to on-demand within 2–5s
- Ideal for: low initial spend, fast validation, dogfooding

Option B — Production Baseline (recommended)
- Cluster: 24x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Min activatable GPUs: 18 (sustained baseline)
- Expected throughput: ~550 reqs/min; p95 ~320ms with batching + KV cache enabled
- Ramp: Month 0–1: activate 18; Month 2–4: scale to 24 as traffic grows; review monthly
- Warm pool / burst: 4-GPU warm pool, 20% burst allowance via on-demand lanes
- Notes: includes autoscaling policy to keep latency under SLO during spikes

Option C — Enterprise Throughput
- Cluster: 60x GPUs (for full production scale)
- Min activatable GPUs: 48
- Ramp: phased over 3–6 months with checkpointed performance gates
- Warm pool / burst: 10–12 GPU warm pool; geo-fallbacks in case of region constraints

Cost guidance: rough ballpark per-token delta between options is driven by utilization and batching — Option A cheapest to start, Option B offers best price/perf for mid growth, Option C reduces unit cost at scale but requires a larger committed spend. We'll include an estimated monthly burn and per-token guidance in the spreadsheet.

Risks & mitigations
- Cold-cache tail latency: mitigated by prefix caching and pre-warm triggers tied to rollout windows
- Model variance/regression: recommend a small canary endpoint with automated quality checks before every scale step

Next steps
1) Quick technical review with Karthik and Grace to confirm kernel/quantization assumptions (I cc'd them).
2) If that checks out, we'll produce a one-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a suggested DocuSign MSA stub for procurement.

Would 2pm PT Thursday for a 30min review work?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Steph — quick notes after scanning the spreadsheet and target profiles:

1) Model/kernel assumptions
- Quantized 70B on 8-bit looks good; with our fused attention kernels and continuous batching we should hit p95 under 350ms on A100-class with the right batch size tuning.

2) Min-activatable GPUs
- For Option B: you can probably reduce the min-activatable from 18→16 by: tighter batching config, slightly higher token-per-batch cap, and enabling hot-KV cache for the most common prefixes. That assumes you accept a 5–8% increase in per-token lat variance during small spike scenarios.

3) Warm-pool sizing
- Warm pool of 4 GPUs is reasonable. For better burst recovery we can implement an anticipatory pre-warm trigger (traffic-based) to bring warm pool to 6 GPUs during scheduled rollouts. Recovery time to full burst (cold→hot) is ~3–6s for our on-demand path; with warm pool it's ~0.8–1.5s.

4) Ramp timeline realism
- Week-level canary OK for small tests. For full Production Baseline, recommend monthly checkpoints (reliability, cost, quality) before adding >20% GPUs.

I'll add a one-page tech note and updated numbers to the spreadsheet (reducing min baseline in Option B to 16) and send back.

-karthik
Principal Infra Architect | Redwood Inference
